title: Sandbox backend construction boundary
description: Only backend resolution constructs a sandbox backend. Tinman chooses the backend for the platform it runs on, so a launch path naming a concrete backend has decided the platform question for itself and will keep deciding it wrongly on the next platform. Discharged by the construction-boundary checker in verification support, which scans the implementation tree for construction expressions naming the type and reports any outside the permitted set. Attested by the @contract scenario in features/sandbox-backend-selection.feature.
rationale: Resolution existed, carried a macOS variant and an unsupported-backend error, and had no caller: all four launch paths named the Bubblewrap backend directly, so the resolver was verified as a function while no operator could reach it. On macOS that is a clean compile, a successful launch attempt and a confusing failure when a binary is missing, where the honest answer is the unsupported-backend error the enum already carries. Bounding construction over the tree is what makes the second backend one edit rather than four, and it covers a launch path added later that nobody remembers to route.
